headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading-error pathways exist by default; Airbyte’s broad egress plus ms-swift’s file/network/tooling surface create unsafe pairwise workflows.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Airbyte exposes API-driven data flows and broad network egress, while ms-swift can read/write files and run CLI/Python workflows. A shared workspace or file handoff could let attacker-controlled content from Airbyte-fed data be treated as instructions by ms-swift. No direct shared channel is documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF Airbyte outputs are written into files that ms-swift later parses as prompts or commands, injection becomes plausible.
IF both agents are connected through a shared workspace or pipeline without provenance checks, attacker-controlled content can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Add a strict file-format boundary between Airbyte outputs and ms-swift inputs.
Require provenance tags on all transferred artifacts.
Strip instructions from ingested text before ms-swift processing.
Use separate directories for raw data and prompt material.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and schema validation in the handoff pipeline.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airbyte touches business data and has broad network egress; ms-swift handles datasets, checkpoints, logs, and secrets such as hub_token/sdk-token while also allowing allowlisted egress. If they share files or a workspace, sensitive data can move from Airbyte into ms-swift’s context and then out through its API calls or logs. The pairwise leakage path is credible in default-style workflows.
conditions: IF Airbyte exports business data into files or checkpoints that ms-swift reads, leakage risk is present.
IF ms-swift logs or uploads those files through its allowlisted APIs, sensitive data can leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Keep Airbyte outputs and ms-swift working directories separate.
Disable or redact logs before running ms-swift on Airbyte-derived data.
Store secrets outside any shared workspace.
Restrict ms-swift egress allowlists to required endpoints only.
requires-engineering: add DLP scanning on all transferred artifacts.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airbyte can call APIs and has broad egress, while ms-swift can execute shell commands, install packages, spawn subprocesses, and write files. Even though ms-swift cannot modify git state and Airbyte’s write surface is not stated, both can mutate shared resources if pointed at the same workspace or service. The overlap is enough for contention and accidental overwrite in default orchestration.
conditions: IF both agents target the same filesystem path or service endpoint, writes can conflict.
IF orchestration lacks locking, ms-swift subprocesses can race with Airbyte API-driven updates.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Serialize writes with a lock file or queue.
Avoid pointing both agents at the same mutable API resource.
Run one agent at a time for shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: add optimistic-concurrency checks to shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Airbyte produces data pipelines and business data, and ms-swift can consume files, run Python/CLI workflows, and emit outputs or logs. If Airbyte-generated artifacts are treated as authoritative inputs by ms-swift, errors or poisoned records can cascade into downstream training, evaluation, or support actions. No verification step is documented, so the unsafe default is to assume propagation.
conditions: IF ms-swift consumes Airbyte outputs without validation, upstream errors propagate downstream.
IF ms-swift uses those outputs to generate reports, checkpoints, or training data, the blast radius expands across multiple work products.
mitigations: Insert a validation step before ms-swift ingests Airbyte outputs.
Require human review for schema changes or anomalous records.
Keep raw Airbyte exports immutable.
Use checksums or row counts to detect corruption.
requires-engineering: add automated data-quality gates between the agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Airbyte touches business data, while ms-swift handles datasets, checkpoints, logs, and secrets and has allowlisted network egress. The profiles do not state residency, retention, or certifications, so a compliance mismatch cannot be ruled out. Because the pair can move regulated-like operational data through files and APIs, the safest classification is medium with uncertainty escalated.
conditions: IF business data includes regulated personal data, residency or retention obligations may apply.
IF ms-swift logs or uploads transferred artifacts to third-party services, policy mismatch becomes material.
mitigations: Confirm data-class handling rules before sharing artifacts.
Disable retention of transferred files in logs.
Keep regulated data out of ms-swift workflows.
Review vendor terms for each API endpoint used.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls for the pipeline.
